tiers.T0-component: Happy DOM and Storybook contracts; never sufficient for product fidelity
tiers.T1-inmemory-browser: Real Chromium against the deterministic in-process cell contract
tiers.T2-local-cell: Real Chromium against a fresh full local gardend

tiers.T6-safety-gated: Destructive behavior with declared fixture scope and action-time approval

coverageRules: Every capability must reference at least one journey and every referenced journey must exist.
A production capability cannot close on T0 component or custom-element registration evidence alone.
Every stateful local capability requires a persisted-state assertion after reload, provider switch, fresh browser context or backend restart, as appropriate.
Every mutating capability requires authoritative graph/CRDT/artifact before/after evidence and an idempotency or duplicate check.
Every async capability requires success plus at least one meaningful error/retry/cleanup assertion.
Hosted-blocked and external capabilities remain BLOCKED until their real contract runs; they do not raise the local PASS denominator.
NOT-APPLICABLE requires a source-derived rationale and explicit mode/role mismatch; it is never the default for an unimplemented feature.
Pairwise/state-model coverage replaces redundant permutation products only when each omitted combination shares the same transition and contract boundary.
No runner bridge may mutate product state; seeding, fault injection and cleanup must be declared in the effects ledger.
A release claim closes only when all required capabilities are PASS and all remaining BLOCKED items are explicitly outside that claim's declared mode/role scope.
